requirement:
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.outline_selectors` has one clause: "Habeas uses the TBV outline selector grammar ... for source addresses." It has no implementation roots, and I found no structural obligation that needs one.

The clause could be read as requiring a particular library or parser. I don't think it does. It names a grammar, which is a syntax for addresses. The detailed rules (path segments, `kind[name]`, `kind@hash`, `#N` disambiguation, percent-encoding, no line numbers) are in the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`. That requirement is cited, not refined here, so it gives context and nothing more.

As a test, take an alternative Habeas that parses and prints source addresses with its own hand-written code instead of the TBV SDK. It accepts and produces exactly the same selector strings. It still "uses the grammar for source addresses", and no one could tell it apart from the original through its behavior. The clause therefore constrains observable address syntax, not a prescribed library, type, signature or delegation. Which code implements the grammar is left to the implementer.

The requirement has test edges (seven nodes) for the behavioral side. Test adequacy is outside this assessment.

behavioral: `requirements.references.outline_selectors` has one observable obligation. Habeas must use the TBV outline selector grammar for source addresses. The grammar's own rules belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, so I did not reassess them here.

The obligation is covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reading_paths]`.
- It builds `OutlineData` addresses with an opaque path, so the path is never read.
- It accepts grammar-valid selectors: the empty selector, `fn[kept]` and `mod[a%2Fb]/fn[kept]`. It asserts that the path and selector are kept unchanged.
- It rejects grammar-invalid selectors: an unterminated `fn[missing`, a malformed percent escape in `fn[bad%ZZ]`, and a leading slash in `/fn[kept]`.

The following tests also carry `{test}` references to the subject. They exercise the grammar that source addresses use, and each assertion checks the expected selector form.
- `markdown_tests.rs#fn[paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges]` checks anonymous `kind@<12 hex>` segments that resolve back to their nodes.
- `tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` checks named and nested segments, percent-encoding, `#N` disambiguation, the empty selector, and rejection of an ambiguous selector.
- `tests.rs#fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` checks the hashed anonymous form and `#N` disambiguation.
- `tests.rs#fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` checks the `line` selector special case.
- `tests.rs#fn[anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits]` checks that a selector built from the identity hash survives an edit to a descendant.
- `tests.rs#fn[profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent]` checks that a missing selector and a malformed one are reported as different errors.

I found no untested behavioral obligation and no marking gap.

text: An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
